lines.text: Arjun's placement FAQ bot has one question from a student, and fifty stored answers, each one a vector. Which answer is closest in meaning?
Picture two vectors as arrows. Cosine similarity measures the angle between them, and ignores how long they are.
Same direction scores one. A right angle scores zero: nothing in common. Opposite directions score minus one.
Forty-five degrees lands in between, at about zero point seven one.
The formula is short: the dot product, divided by the two lengths multiplied together.
Take three, four and six, eight. They point the same way, so even with different lengths, the score is exactly one.
Now the trick. Scale every vector to length one, just once. After that, cosine similarity is simply the dot product.
So stack all fifty answers into one matrix, multiply by the question, and you get fifty scores at once.
Sort them, keep the top three. That is vector search, in a few lines of NumPy.
The answers are embedded once and saved. Only the question is new each time.
One warning: a score is for ranking. Zero point eight two does not mean eighty-two percent correct.
So the line to remember: vector search is a dot product and a sort. Everything after that is about speed.
